text_blocks.snippet: Gestational diabetes, which develops during pregnancy, is diagnosed through blood tests that assess how well the body processes glucose. The diagnostic process typically involves an initial glucose challenge test, followed by an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) if the initial test is abnormal.

list.snippet: This test is usually performed between 24 and 28 weeks of pregnancy, though it may be done earlier for women with risk factors.
It involves drinking a sugary liquid (containing 50 grams of glucose) and having a blood sample taken one hour later.
